lines.text: Haul Control to all couriers — the Vane Street corridor is open again. Lanes four through nine, keep it under two hundred.
We have a manifest mismatch on the Kessel drop. If that box is warm, it is not my problem.
PULL UP, COURIER. PULL UP. YOU ARE INSIDE THE STACK.
Shift change in ten. Whoever is on the roof at Ardent, the beacon is out again. Still.
Somebody has parked a freighter across two of my lanes. I am told this is temporary. I am told a lot of things.
Weather is closing the upper approach at Pale Terrace. If you are booked up there, you are now booked somewhere else.
Courier, your parcel is logged and the pad is holding for you. Try not to make them wait.
Logged. Clock's running. Try to look like you've done this before.
That's on your manifest now. Whatever it is.
Confirmed. Lane's clear as far as I can see, which is not far.
You've got it. Sealed, weighed, and none of my business.
Accepted. They asked for someone reliable. I sent you anyway.
Booked. Take the high lane, the low one's a car park.
On the board and off my desk. Go.
Nice run. Credits are clearing now. Don't spend it all in the Ribs.
Signed for. Money's moving. Slowly, but it's moving.
Delivered and closed. That's one thing today that went where it was supposed to.
Paid. They didn't complain, which from them is a compliment.
Clean drop. I'm marking you as competent. Don't make me change it.
Received in one piece. Credits inbound. Enjoy the four minutes before you need them.
Logged, paid, forgotten. That's the job.
Done. There's more where that came from, unfortunately.
